polymer.basis: Polyvinyl chloride is sold as a powder, and its producers publish what a powder has: Vynova's S5702 sheet gives a bulk density of 570 kg/m3 and no polymer density, and OxyChem's own Vinyl Handbook covers apparent bulk density only. The one figure found in a producer document is a specific gravity of 1.4 in SCGC's safety data sheet (Section 9), with no test method beside it, which is not a density range this database would bound an estimate with. Both columns therefore say Not recorded, as PCL's do (R052, R057). Unplasticised PVC is amorphous and has no melting point; a plasticised compound says so on its grade.
